data.title: Export / save / copy-css with a live float: stamp it first?

data.body:
Raised by the PM-7 review (see PM-7's review comment for the full reasoning). PM-7 added a floating paste that is deliberately NOT part of the document until stamped (it never bumps dirtyDoc, it is never in history). Every context change stamps it first — tool switch, mode switch, cell size, focus enter/exit/move — EXCEPT the three export escapes in src/main.ts: doSave (pattern.json), doExportPng, doCopyCss. Export mid-paste therefore omits what is on screen.

Coherent as designed, so this is a product call, not a bug: should an explicit export/save stamp the float first (one line each: commitFloatFirst() at the top of the three functions), or keep ignoring it? Needs a human decision on which is less surprising.

Deliberately out of scope either way: autosave. It must NOT stamp — firing a document mutation from a debounced timer the user never triggered is worse than the gap.

Human decision (forrest): current behavior is correct as-is — export/save/copy-css do not stamp a live floating paste; the float is not part of the document until deliberately stamped, and all context changes already stamp first. No code change. Closing.

Human reversed the earlier keep-as-is decision: fix it. Scope per the PM-7 reviewer's analysis: doSave / doExportPng / doCopyCss stamp a live float first (explicit user actions export what's on screen); autosave deliberately does NOT stamp (a debounced timer must never mutate the document).
